chunks: And in the narration of Ḥamdān ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Walīd, from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān.
He said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: For what reason did the inheritance become
for the male, the like of the share of two females
He said: Because of what Allah has assigned for her of the dowry.

key_terms.الصَّدَاقِ: the dowry obligated for the woman in marriage
key_terms.عِلَّةٍ: the underlying reason or legal cause
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: the legal rule that a male receives the share of two females

ai.seo_question: Why does a male inherit the share of two females in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal rationale for the inheritance rule by linking the male's larger share to the financial obligation placed upon him in marriage. The Imam عليه السلام explains that the woman's dowry is among the reasons for this differential allocation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5756 - In the narration of Hamdan ibn Al-Husayn from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Walid from Ibn Bukayr from Abdullah ibn Sinan,
he said: "I asked Abu Abdullah (as), 'For what reason is the inheritance for the male
equal to the share of two females?'
Imam (as) replied: 'Because Allah (swt) has allocated the dowry (ṣadaq) for her.'"
